data_quality_summary.explanation: We identified plausible benchmark-size CUSIPs for 4 of 5 obligors (Steward has no public muni debt, confirmed). However, none of the public, free, scrape-accessible sources (municipalbonds.com, bondview.com, EMMA, Bond Buyer) expose historical CUSIP-level trade prices/yields at the snapshot dates without a subscription or active anti-scrape blocking. municipalbonds.com only shows ~5 most-recent trades behind a registration wall, despite indicating hundreds-to-thousands of historical trades. bondview.com returns 403 to anonymous WebFetch even with Chrome fingerprint. EMMA's Security/SecurityDetails URL paths returned 404 (their actual security IDs are opaque GUIDs behind a CUSIP-disclaimer interstitial we couldn't get past programmatically without an interactive Chromium). The MSRB explicitly prohibits scraping per their TOU. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT attempt to compute pair-trade P&L from this data. Use literature-derived spread proxies instead (e.g., AA hospital ~+50 to +75 bps over MMD AAA, BBB hospital ~+100-150 bps, CCC distressed ~+800-1500 bps), anchored to the verified MSRB-published BVAL AAA Callable benchmark curve which we DO have for both dates.

obligors.name: Steward Health Care
obligors.verification_status: UNVERIFIED (confirmed no public muni bonds exist)
obligors.notes: Steward was converted from non-profit Caritas Christi Health Care to for-profit in November 2010 when Cerberus Capital Management completed its leveraged buyout. As a for-profit since 2010, Steward had NO ability to issue tax-exempt 501(c)(3) revenue bonds through conduit authorities — that's the whole structural reason municipal-credit Signal OS would not have a workflow path on it. Its outstanding debt consisted of (a) the 2016 $1.25B sale-leaseback with Medical Properties Trust (which is corporate REIT debt of MPT, not Steward muni paper), (b) a $350M convertible bond Cerberus took at 2020 exit, and (c) private credit / DIP loans. Steward filed Chapter 11 May 6, 2024. NO MUNI BOND CUSIP EXISTS — this is the correct outcome for our pilot (validates that survivorship-/ineligibility-screening at the outset would have excluded Steward from a muni-credit signal universe anyway). Sources: Wikipedia 'Steward Health Care System'; pestakeholder.org reports; Brookings 'Lessons from the collapse of Steward Health Care'.

obligors.notes: Tower Health is the most useful obligor in the pilot for showing yield differentiation — even bracketing trades demonstrate yields 800-1500 bps over AAA benchmark, validating the literature CCC/distressed spread range. At snapshot (Dec 2022), Tower was BB- but Fitch had just downgraded to CCC+ (Sept 2022) — bonds were almost certainly already trading at 10-15% yield. At endpoint (March 2025), post-distressed-exchange (Sept 2024 closed), this specific 2017-Series CUSIP may have been part of the exchange and trade activity may be light. Recommend treating Tower's 2022→2025 yield change as approximately +500 to +1000 bps WIDENING peak-to-trough, NOT a clean compute against this CUSIP.

recommendations_for_pair_trade_p_and_l.rationale: Without CUSIP-level trade prices on the two target dates, we cannot compute realized total return for any of the 4 obligors with public bonds. We have only the benchmark curve at both dates (HIGH confidence) and one bracketing distressed-trade observation for Tower Health.
next_steps_if_real_p_and_l_is_required: Option A (gold-standard): Subscribe to Bloomberg Terminal or LSEG/Refinitiv TM3 MMD; pull historical BVAL evaluated prices for each CUSIP on 2022-12-31 and 2025-03-31. ~$24K/yr.

Option B (cheaper, manual): Use a headless Chrome session (Playwright/Selenium) to navigate EMMA after clicking the CUSIP disclaimer, then parse the trade history tab. EMMA's TOU prohibits this for bulk/database creation but allows interactive viewing. Per-CUSIP manual work ~10 min × 4 obligors = ~40 min.

Option C (cheapest, used here): Use MMD AAA benchmark + sector spread proxies. Reasonable for relative comparisons across obligors but introduces ±10-30 bps noise per obligor. ACCEPTABLE for the pilot — DO NOT claim point-estimate alpha precision.
Recommended for current pilot (5 obligors): Option C with explicit ±30 bps confidence intervals on the spread proxies, anchored to the HIGH-confidence MSRB BVAL benchmark.
